network.overall_strategy: The network separates robust abiotic construction of the proline scaffold from the unresolved problem of L-selectivity. A surface discharge step generates a reusable HCN/formaldehyde hub pool; from that pool, the mechanistically explicit Patel cyanosulfidic branch proceeds through acrylonitrile, beta-aminopropionitrile, and pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile, while hydrothermal HCN/HCHO/NH3 chemistry, thermal HCHO/NH3 condensation, the molybdate/clay HCHO/NH2OH system, formamide irradiation, and direct electric discharge all provide parallel entries to a common proline pool. Ten distinct pathways arise by combining the discharge hub with downstream routes and by retaining independent direct routes. Because no supplied study demonstrates strong abiotic L-selectivity, the final proline-to-L-proline step is included explicitly as a speculative post-synthetic enrichment module.

reactions.name: Electric-discharge generation of HCN and formaldehyde

conditions.other: spark discharge over CH4/N2/H2O with NH3 under anoxic conditions; the carbonyl pool is simplified here to formaldehyde

reactions.mechanism: Plasma activation of reduced gases forms nitriles and carbonyls; condensation into the aqueous phase yields an HCN/carbonyl inventory represented here by HCN and formaldehyde.
reactions.reasoning: This node is a hub-building abstraction of Miller-type discharge chemistry. Ring et al. directly observed proline in CH4/N2/H2O/trace NH3 discharge mixtures, making upstream formation of HCN and carbonyl compounds chemically reasonable; silicate vessel effects can materially change product distributions (Ring et al., 1972; Criado-Reyes et al., 2021). The specific globally reducing atmosphere is contested, so this step is best assigned to local or transient reduced settings rather than the average Hadean atmosphere (Trail et al., 2011; Rugheimer and Rimmer, 2019).

reactions.name: HCN-acetylene coupling to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: UV-exposed shallow pond or shoreline film; cyanide-rich and anoxic

reactions.mechanism: C-C bond formation between cyanide-derived carbon and acetylene gives the activated unsaturated nitrile acrylonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. used HCN/acetylene chemistry to access acrylonitrile as the entry point to the proline branch of cyanosulfidic protometabolism. This is one of the best-resolved prebiotic C-C bond-forming steps toward the proline skeleton, although it presupposes co-availability of HCN, acetylene, and suitable Cu photoredox chemistry (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Ammonolysis of acrylonitrile to beta-aminopropionitrile
reactions.mechanism: Ammonia adds across the activated C=C of acrylonitrile to give the beta-amino nitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. reported high conversion of acrylonitrile to beta-aminopropionitrile by ammonia addition, making this one of the experimentally strongest individual transformations in the prebiotic proline branch (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Cyanosulfidic cyclization to pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile

conditions.other: UV irradiation; this reaction compresses the experimentally tracked 3-aminopropanal, cyanohydrin, thioamide, and gamma-butyrothiolactam substeps

reactions.mechanism: Photoreduction of beta-aminopropionitrile gives 3-aminopropanal, cyanohydrin formation and thioamide cyclization generate a cyclic sulfur intermediate, and reductive cyanation furnishes the cyclic alpha-aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. identified 3-aminopropanal, cyanohydrin, thioamide, and gamma-butyrothiolactam intermediates en route to pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile. This node compresses those experimentally supported substeps to maintain network size; it is the best-resolved prebiotic route to the proline skeleton, but it still depends on carefully ordered HCN, HS-, Cu, and UV chemistry (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile to proline

conditions.other: prolonged wet conditions or mild geothermal cycling

reactions.mechanism: Nitrile hydration followed by hydrolysis converts the alpha-aminonitrile to the carboxylic acid.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. stopped experimentally at the immediate proline aminonitrile, so hydrolysis to free proline is chemically standard but not the quantified endpoint of that paper. The inference is nonetheless consistent with the broader hydrolysis-based detection of proline-releasing precursors in other route families (Patel et al., 2015; Fox and Windsor, 1970; Hatanaka and Egami, 1977).

reactions.name: Hydrothermal HCN-formaldehyde-ammonia synthesis of proline

conditions.other: reducing, anoxic hydrothermal fluid; rapid quench and mixing favored

reactions.mechanism: Hot cyanide-carbonyl-ammonium chemistry generates amino-acid precursors, with minor ring-forming branches yielding proline.
reactions.reasoning: Hennet et al. detected proline at about 150 C from HCN, formaldehyde, and ammonium under hydrothermal conditions with geologically motivated mineral assemblages; Marshall likewise supported rapid hot amino-acid chemistry in related systems (Hennet et al., 1992; Marshall, 1994). The extrapolation is limited by unrealistically high precursor concentrations and by thermal destruction, which becomes severe at higher temperature unless residence times are short and reducing conditions are maintained (Bada et al., 1995; Yanagawa and Kobayashi, 1997).

reactions.name: Thermal formaldehyde-ammonia condensation and hydrolytic release of proline

conditions.pressure: sealed aqueous phase, near-ambient to mildly elevated
conditions.other: heated concentrated HCHO/NH3; proline is inferred after hydrolysis of the thermal product

reactions.mechanism: Repeated C-C and C-N condensations in heated formaldehyde-ammonia mixtures produce hydrolysable precursors that release proline on hydrolysis.
reactions.reasoning: Fox and Windsor reported proline after hydrolysis of heated HCHO/NH3 mixtures around 185 C. The route is catalyst-free but mechanistically unresolved, and the evidence is for proline-releasing material rather than a well-quantified free proline pool before hydrolysis; related historical critiques underline the importance of hydrolysis controls in low-yield systems (Fox and Windsor, 1970; Wolman et al., 1971).

reactions.name: Molybdate-clay-directed HCHO-NH2OH synthesis of proline

conditions.other: initial pH about 5.5, sealed under N2 for about 7 d, hydrolysis before analysis

reactions.mechanism: Oxime and cyanide-generating condensations in a multimetal clay medium build hydrolysable C-N oligomers; molybdate redirects selectivity toward proline.
reactions.reasoning: Hatanaka and Egami showed a strong molybdate-dependent increase in proline among the hydrolyzed amino-acid products, with proline reaching 2.75 mol% of analyzed residues at 10^-2 M molybdate. The chemistry is experimentally impressive but not uniquely Mo-catalyzed, because the active medium also contains multiple transition metals and clays; moreover, both hydroxylamine supply and high molybdate activity are geochemically difficult to justify under anoxic conditions (Hatanaka and Egami, 1977; Scott et al., 2008).

reactions.name: Particle-irradiated formamide synthesis of proline

conditions.other: high-energy proton or cosmic-ray equivalent irradiation of neat or highly concentrated formamide on meteorite-rich mineral surfaces

reactions.mechanism: Irradiation fragments formamide into HCN, NH3, and radical C/N species that recombine through Strecker-like and radical channels to amino acids including proline.
reactions.reasoning: Saladino et al. directly identified proline in irradiated formamide plus meteorite powders. This branch is experimentally secure as a source of proline, but its ring-forming mechanism remains unresolved and the need for neat or highly concentrated formamide is a major prebiotic limitation; in the present schema it is represented as a surface-delivery or impact-associated irradiation context (Saladino et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Direct electric-discharge synthesis of proline

conditions.other: spark discharge in a strongly reducing gas mixture under anoxic conditions

reactions.mechanism: Energetic plasma generates nitriles, carbonyls, amines, and complex condensates; minor branch chemistry yields the proline skeleton directly.
reactions.reasoning: Ring et al. directly detected proline in CH4/N2/H2O/trace NH3 discharge mixtures. The yield was low and the ring-forming mechanism unresolved; later work shows that glass or silicate surfaces can materially alter Miller-type product distributions, and the atmospheric redox state needed for this route is geochemically contested on a global scale (Ring et al., 1972; Criado-Reyes et al., 2021; Trail et al., 2011).

reactions.name: Post-synthetic enantioenrichment to L-proline

conditions.other: non-equilibrium adsorption, dissolution, crystallization, or compartmental selection in concentrated pools; unselected material is not explicitly represented

reactions.mechanism: A stereochemically mixed proline pool undergoes physical or chemical selection that enriches the L enantiomer.
reactions.reasoning: This step is explicitly speculative. The supplied literature supports abiotic synthesis of proline but does not demonstrate significant intrinsic L-selective production; UV-ice products are racemic or unresolved, and meteoritic proline includes both enantiomers. Accordingly this node represents an unresolved post-synthetic enrichment module rather than an experimentally established conversion (Munoz Caro et al., 2002; Bernstein et al., 2002; Engel and Nagy, 1982).

pathways.name: Direct cyanosulfidic route
pathways.description: Environmental HCN, acetylene, and ammonia feed the Patel branch through acrylonitrile, beta-aminopropionitrile, and proline aminonitrile; hydrolysis gives proline, followed by speculative L-enrichment.

pathways.name: Discharge-fed cyanosulfidic route
pathways.description: Reduced-atmosphere discharge first generates an HCN/formaldehyde hub; the HCN fraction then feeds the Patel proline-aminonitrile branch, followed by hydrolysis and speculative L-enrichment.

pathways.name: Direct hydrothermal cyanide-carbonyl route
pathways.description: HCN, formaldehyde, and ammonia react in a reducing Fe-S hydrothermal system to give proline, which then enters the speculative L-enrichment module.

pathways.name: Atmosphere-to-vent hydrothermal route
pathways.description: Atmospheric discharge supplies HCN and formaldehyde that are later processed in a hydrothermal Fe-S system, then subjected to speculative L-enrichment.

pathways.name: Direct thermal formaldehyde-ammonia route
pathways.description: Heated HCHO/NH3 chemistry forms hydrolysable proline precursors that yield proline on hydrolysis, followed by speculative L-selection.

pathways.name: Discharge-fed thermal formaldehyde-ammonia route
pathways.description: Electric discharge supplies formaldehyde to the Fox-Windsor thermal condensation network, after which the resulting proline enters the speculative L-enrichment module.

pathways.name: Direct molybdate-clay hydroxylamine route
pathways.description: Concentrated HCHO and NH2OH in a multimetal clay medium yield hydrolysis-released proline, followed by speculative L-enrichment.

pathways.name: Discharge-fed molybdate-clay hydroxylamine route
pathways.description: Atmospherically generated formaldehyde is concentrated into the Hatanaka-Egami molybdate/clay/hydroxylamine surface system, then converted to proline and passed to speculative L-enrichment.

pathways.name: Direct formamide irradiation route
pathways.description: Irradiated formamide in a meteorite-rich surface setting yields proline directly, after which the pool is subjected to the unresolved L-enrichment module.

pathways.name: Direct electric-discharge route
pathways.description: Strongly reducing spark-discharge chemistry gives proline directly as a minor product, which then enters the speculative L-enrichment step.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the closest match to the best-resolved literature route, but rxn_004 is both unbalanced and chemically compressed: the Patel branch requires 3-aminopropanal, cyanohydrin/thioamide chemistry, HS-/UV/Cu conditions, and more than a single HCN addition. rxn_005 is plausible only as aqueous hydrolysis with water input and NH3/NH4+ output, not as a generic biochemical step. rxn_011 remains speculative because no strong abiotic L-selective enrichment to L-proline is established.
suggestions: Expand rxn_004 into explicit Patel-style steps with 3-aminopropanal, cyanohydrin, thioamide/thiolactam intermediates, and HS-/UV/Cu conditions.
Rewrite rxn_005 as balanced aqueous hydrolysis including H2O input and NH3/NH4+ output.
Treat L-enrichment as a separate unresolved module or retarget the network to proline without specified stereochemistry.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Adding rxn_001 makes the branch complete from simple gases, but rxn_001 is unbalanced; RDKit hints that H2 and NH3 coproducts and possibly CO as a co-reactant are missing. The downstream issue remains rxn_004, which collapses the Patel sequence into an impossible one-step cyclization, and rxn_005/rxn_011 are still under-specified. Literature support is qualitative for the route family, not for these exact reaction statements.
suggestions: Balance rxn_001 with explicit coproducts/reactants suggested by RDKit and separate hub formation from downstream chemistry.
Replace rxn_004 with explicit Patel intermediates and required HS-/UV/Cu conditions.
Change rxn_005 and rxn_011 to defined aqueous hydrolysis and explicit, evidence-backed chiral enrichment, or stop at proline.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Hennet-type hydrothermal chemistry does report proline in complex mixtures, but rxn_006 is an impossible one-step stoichiometry and RDKit found no simple small-species fix. The cited literature also uses concentrated HCN/HCHO/NH4+ with mineral redox buffers rather than a bare three-reactant step. rxn_011 leaves the actual L-proline target unresolved.
suggestions: Replace rxn_006 with a multistep hydrothermal precursor network or an empirical product-mixture node tied to measured HCN/HCHO/NH4+ plus mineral conditions.
Add mineral/redox context, temperature/pressure, and quenching/transport explicitly.
Keep the endpoint at proline unless a supported L-enrichment chemistry is supplied.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Conceptually plausible as atmospheric feedstock delivery into hydrothermal processing, but the pathway lacks an explicit transport/concentration step between rxn_001 and rxn_006. rxn_001 is unbalanced; RDKit hints missing H2/NH3 coproducts and possibly CO. rxn_006 is unbalanced with no simple fix, and rxn_011 is speculative. The environment sequence is reasonable in spirit but not chemically explicit enough.
suggestions: Insert dissolution, transport, and concentration steps for HCN and CH2O between atmospheric generation and hydrothermal processing.
Balance rxn_001 with explicit coproducts/reactants suggested by RDKit and replace rxn_006 with a multistep hydrothermal module.
Treat L-enrichment as unresolved rather than a generic biochemical conversion.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Fox-type thermal HCHO/NH3 chemistry supports proline only after hydrolysis of complex thermal products. rxn_007 is heavily unbalanced and the literature does not justify direct CH2O + NH3 -> proline as a single step. The surface/geothermal setting is plausible, but the network should pass through hydrolysable precursor material before any proline node.
suggestions: Insert a hydrolysable precursor or oligomeric intermediate node between HCHO/NH3 heating and proline release.
Add an explicit hydrolysis step and rebalance the net chemistry instead of using a single CH2O unit.
Stop at proline or provide a distinct supported enantioenrichment module.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Using rxn_001 as a formaldehyde source is conceptually fine, but rxn_001 is unbalanced; RDKit hints missing H2/NH3 coproducts and possibly CO. rxn_007 is still an invalid one-step conversion, and the branch omits the concentrated hot-condensation and hydrolysis context of the literature. rxn_011 again does not solve L-selectivity.
suggestions: Balance rxn_001 explicitly and model transport/concentration of discharge-derived formaldehyde into the hot-condensation setting.
Replace rxn_007 with precursor formation plus hydrolysis, not direct proline formation.
Do not encode L-proline production without an evidence-backed chiral step.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This route family is literature-supported, but rxn_008 omits the actual multicomponent conditions that favor proline: molybdate, clays, other metals, controlled pH, heating, and hydrolysis. It is also unbalanced and RDKit found no simple small-species fix. The best proline-selective experimental condition uses high molybdate, which is geochemically hard to justify without a specific concentrating niche.
suggestions: Add explicit catalyst/mineral nodes such as molybdate, kaolinite, montmorillonite, and transition metals, plus hydrolysis.
Model the chemistry as a multistep or empirical product-mixture process rather than CH2O + NH2OH -> proline.
Justify hydroxylamine and high local molybdate sourcing if this branch is retained.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The discharge-fed version provides HCHO from within the network, but rxn_001 remains unbalanced; RDKit hints H2/NH3 coproducts and possibly CO. rxn_008 still collapses a complex molybdate/clay/hydrolysis system into an impossible one-step conversion. Environmental transfer from atmospheric organics to a specialized mineral surface is plausible but under-justified, and rxn_011 remains speculative.
suggestions: Balance rxn_001 explicitly and add transfer/concentration from atmospheric organics to the mineral-rich surface niche.
Expand rxn_008 to include molybdate, clays, other metals, pH, heating, and hydrolysis.
Keep the product as proline unless a supported L-enrichment mechanism is added.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Formamide irradiation with meteorite material can yield proline, but rxn_009 is not a valid one-step stoichiometry and omits the defining context: neat or highly concentrated formamide, meteorite/mineral surfaces, and energetic particle irradiation. Labeling the setting simply surface under-specifies the cited experiments. rxn_011 again lacks experimental support for L-selective enrichment.
suggestions: Specify meteorite/mineral catalyst and irradiation energy explicitly, or move this branch to a dedicated irradiation/extraterrestrial environment.
Break formamide chemistry into smaller precursor steps or represent it as an empirical mixture-generating module.
Do not claim L-proline without a separate chiral enrichment process.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Direct discharge synthesis of proline is literature-aligned as a route family, but rxn_010 is unbalanced and not a chemically explicit reaction. RDKit hints that H2 and NH3 coproducts are missing. The strongly reducing CH4/N2/H2O/NH3 gas regime is also environmentally contested as a global Hadean atmosphere, though it could apply locally. rxn_011 leaves the L-proline target unsupported.
suggestions: Balance rxn_010 with explicit coproducts such as those hinted by RDKit and consider using a discharge-product-mixture node.
State the atmospheric scenario as local or transient reducing conditions if that is the intent.
Separate any L-enrichment from the discharge synthesis branch.

evaluation.network_feedback: Conceptually, the network is well aligned with the literature: it covers the major experimentally discussed proline route families and correctly treats L-selectivity as unresolved. The graph is connected and molecule IDs are used consistently. However, as a reaction network it is not valid enough because only rxn_002, rxn_003, and rxn_011 are balanced as written; rxn_001, rxn_004, rxn_005, rxn_006, rxn_007, rxn_008, rxn_009, and rxn_010 are deterministically UNBALANCED. To correct them, rxn_001 needs explicit coproduct/reactant accounting; RDKit hints H2 and NH3 as products and possibly CO as a reactant. rxn_010 likewise needs H2/NH3 coproduct accounting, rxn_005 needs explicit hydrolysis stoichiometry with water and ammonia accounting, and rxn_004, rxn_006, rxn_007, rxn_008, and rxn_009 should be expanded into proper multistep chemistry because the balance check found no simple small-species fix for them. The Patel-inspired branch is the strongest literature match, but rxn_004 collapses required HS-/UV/Cu-mediated intermediates into an impossible single step and rxn_005 should be explicit aqueous hydrolysis rather than a biochemical placeholder. The hydrothermal, thermal HCHO/NH3, molybdate-clay, formamide, and direct discharge branches are all real route families in the literature, but here they are encoded as mass-nonconserving one-step conversions to proline. Finally, rxn_011 is only a speculative post-synthetic enantioenrichment module; the supplied literature does not demonstrate a strong abiotic synthesis of L-proline. Overall, this is a useful literature map but not yet a chemically valid synthesis network for L-proline.
